clinician.final_diagnosis: COVID-19 diagnosed through an imaging study of the retina.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old healthy male anesthetist, with recent COVID-19 patient exposure, presented with sudden temporal relative scotoma in the left eye. Initial ophthalmic exams were unremarkable. Swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) revealed a hyperreflective band at the level of ganglion cell and inner plexiform layers, sparing the outer retina. Fluorescein angiography showed no leakage or exudation. Routine blood tests were normal, and SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR was negative. Follow-up retinal imaging 30 days later showed the hyperreflective lesions with increased intensity. The diagnosis of COVID-19 was made based on these retinal imaging findings.
